predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: the fief granted to Baldwin I: 'Fief granted to Count Baldwin I in 862'

successors.name: Duchy of Burgundy
successors.text: the whole county: 'From 1384, the county was politically united to the Duchy of Burgundy'

ledger.x: 862: Baldwin I becomes the first Count of Flanders.
898: Baldwin II integrates Artois into Flanders.
1167: Philip of Alsace and Elisabeth inherit Vermandois.
1185: the Treaty of Boves gives the king Amiens and Montdidier.
1186: Philip cedes Vermandois to the king.
1264: Guy of Dampierre becomes Marquis of Namur.
1305: Namur leaves the count of Flanders.
1305: Lille, Douai and Orchies pass to the French crown.
1305: the Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge ends the Franco-Flemish War; Flanders keeps its independence 'as a fief of the French kingdom' and pays large fines.
1322: Louis I unites Nevers with Flanders.
1357: the Peace of Ath gives Louis II Antwerp and Mechelen.
1384: Flanders passes to the Dukes of Burgundy.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Flanders and Hainault
wars.outcome: Guy's side lost at Walcheren in 1253 and Guy was taken prisoner; by the mediation of Louis IX he was ransomed in 1256.

wars.name: Franco-Flemish War
wars.outcome: French victory at Furnes (1297) and conquest of Flanders (1300); Flemish victory at the Golden Spurs (11 July 1302); French victory at Mons-en-Pévèle (1304).

wars.name: Flemish revolt of 1323-1328
wars.outcome: Tax unrest became an uprising in 1323 led by Nicolaas Zannekin; the rebels took Nieuwpoort, Veurne, Ypres and Kortrijk and captured Louis; Charles IV intervened and the Peace of Arques was sealed on 26 April 1326; the rebels were defeated by the French royal…

wars.name: Uprising of Jacob van Artevelde at Ghent
wars.outcome: Edward III's wool boycott helped spark a 1337 uprising under Artevelde; Louis I fled his lands in 1339 and never returned.

wars.name: Louis II's invasion of Brabant
wars.outcome: Louis captured Brussels in August 1356 and seized the duchy; at the Peace of Ath (4 June 1357) he kept the Brabant title for life and reclaimed Mechelen and gained Antwerp for the county.

wars.name: Ghent revolt (White Hoods)
wars.outcome: The revolt broke out in 1379 and continued beyond Louis of Male's death on 30 January 1384.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines in the pages opened; the Imperial and royal fiefs overlap east and west of the Scheldt.
The Lille-Douai-Orchies line is fixed by the treaty of 23 June 1305 and the 1369 return, and the Peace of Ath (4 June 1357) fixes the Antwerp-Mechelen holdings; every other frontier stays soft.
